chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn Uqda said to us: My father Muhammad ibn al-Mufadhdhal ibn Ibrahim ibn Qays ibn Rumana narrated to me from his book in the month of Rajab in the year two hundred and sixty-five, saying: Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhl narrated to us, saying: Tha'laba ibn Maymun, Abu Ishaq, narrated to us from Isa ibn A'yun, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:

The Sufyani is of the inevitable ones, and his emergence is in Rajab, and from the beginning of his emergence to its end is fifteen months, six months he fights in them, and when he conquers the five districts, he rules for nine months, and he does not add to them a single day.

key_terms.السُّفْيَانِيُّ: The Sufyani, a specific figure in Shia eschatology who emerges before the appearance of the Mahdi.
key_terms.الْكُورَ الْخَمْسَ: The five districts or regions, referring to specific geographical areas conquered by the Sufyani.
key_terms.الْمُحْتَوَمِ: The inevitable/destined one, referring to an event or person whose occurrence is preordained.
key_terms.رَجَبَ: The seventh month of the Islamic lunar calendar.

ai.seo_question: What is the timeline and duration of the Sufyani's emergence according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), transmitted via al-Nu'mani’s chain, establishes the emergence of al-Sufyani as a fixed eschatological sign (al-Mahmud) occurring in Rajab, a timeline corroborated by various Shia hadith collections. The specific duration of fifteen months—divided into six months of warfare and nine months of dominion over the 'five districts' (al-Kur al-Khams)—provides a structured framework for understanding the pre-Mahdi political landscape. This period is significant in Shia scholarship as the time of preparation and consolidation before the appearance of Imam al-Mahdi.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (1) Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Sa’eed bin Oqda narrated from Muhammad bin al-Mufadhdhal bin Ibraheem bin Qays from al-Hasan bin Ali bin Fadhdhal from Tha’laba bin Maymoon Abu Iss’haq from Eessa bin A’yun that Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (as) had said:

“The rising of as-Sufyani is an inevitable matter. He will rise in the month of Rajab. It will take, since his rising until his end, fifteen months. He will fight for six months. When he conquers the five districts, he will rule for nine months no more no less.”
